notes:
ABSORBED EDITOR-W0 (2026-07-25, owner call): the de-risk spike is removed. Its output was a findings note, not working software, and it meant doing the integration twice — the decision is already made (CM6, ADR-0010 in W7), so there is nothing left for a spike to decide. W1 behind a flag IS the same experiment, except the code survives and tests catch what the spike would have found by hand.

The spike's checks become acceptance criteria here, in this order — they are the risky seams and they are verified FIRST, before the rest of the swap is polished:

1. FOCUS INTERPLAY WITH XTERM. The whole ownership machine is focus-based (tabs.ts:407-417 focus-bounce, :432-467 global keydown redirect) while CM6 manages focus itself. Verify: the bounce still keeps typing in the editor when the editor owns input; clicking the xterm live region still keeps focus there; rootContains() still resolves through CM6's nested DOM at BOTH call sites (:413 and :457-464).
2. KEYMAP PRECEDENCE. CM6's defaultKeymap binds Enter and Escape. Without Prec.highest, Enter inserts a newline and Ctrl-C stops interrupting the shell — a silent regression in the two most-used keys at a prompt. (Detailed in W2; W1 must not ship a state where they are wrong.)
3. IME COMPOSITION. Zero coverage exists today. The document-level keydown redirect can destroy composition state.
4. HIT-TESTING. document.elementFromPoint over the editor card must return the editor, not .xterm-link-layer — this is the nocx-4ff.16 bug and nocx-0oc says the z-index rule it was fixed with is not actually in the stylesheet.
5. GEOMETRY UNDER visibility:hidden. CM6 measures its own layout, and _shownOnce keeps the editor hidden that way for most of its life. Assert correct size and focusability on the show following a hide.
6. WKWEBVIEW, NOT ONLY CHROMIUM. Playwright drives Chromium; the shipping runtime is WKWebView (AD-3). IME and focus findings are either reproduced on the real WebView or explicitly recorded as unverified — not silently assumed.

If any of these turns out to need a different migration shape, that is a finding on nocx-2gf and W1 is re-planned — same outcome the spike would have produced, with working code already in hand.

title: EDITOR-W5: rebuild the test surface (browser mode decision + first IME coverage)
description:
Spec W5. Rewrite the hit-testing assertions in e2e/command-editor.spec.ts that expect elementFromPoint to return a TEXTAREA, plus clipboard.spec.ts:147 and click-focus.spec.ts:37-45 which assume the active element carries .nocx-editor-input and read selectionStart/selectionEnd. Delete the already-dead submit-button test (see nocx-m7x).

jsdom performs no layout, so every CM6 behaviour depending on measurement — caret coordinates, popup placement, wrapping — is untestable there. That forces the nocx-foz decision rather than leaving it implicit.

Add the first IME composition coverage this repo has ever had: the document-level keydown redirect at tabs.ts:432 can destroy composition state silently.
acceptance_criteria: e2e suite green against the new surface. A composition sequence produces the composed text exactly once. nocx-foz closed with a decision either way and its reasoning recorded.

title: STORE-5: settings registry on DocumentStore — the screen is generated
description:
ADR-0011 + nocx-1ei. Replace internal/config's untyped Get(key) (any, error) / Set(key string, value any) bag, which cannot enumerate what settings exist, their types, defaults or validation — and therefore cannot drive a generated screen.

Typed declarations carrying key, default, label, description, section, validation, data class and control kind. Because Go cannot hold differently-typed declarations in one slice directly, expose a non-generic descriptor interface for enumeration alongside typed keys for get/set. Retires the config Stub (nocx-jap), and makes 'Don't show again' on the OSC 52 gate mean what it says (nocx-3cc).

A secret-class setting generates an editor whose operations are set, delete and exists — never get.
acceptance_criteria: The settings screen is rendered from declarations, not hand-maintained. A user decision survives restart. Adding a setting requires touching one declaration site. No secret-class setting exposes a read operation.
close_reason:
STORE-5 landed across three workers: the typed registry (internal/settings), the generated screen (frontend/src/settings.ts), and the wiring (7 JSON-RPC methods in ws.go, composition-root pairing in app.go). internal/config and its untyped Get(key) (any, error) bag are DELETED, not adapted — that retires nocx-jap.

Acceptance checked rather than taken on report. Screen is generated: it switches on decl.control and groups by decl.section, with no literal setting key anywhere, so a new declaration renders with zero frontend change. A decision made in the screen survives restart via DocumentStore. Adding a setting is one MustRegister* call.

No secret-class read exists, structurally: the registry exposes SecretSet/SecretDelete/SecretExists and there is no GetSecret method at all; GetAll skips secret-class keys; Reset refuses them; settings.set rejects a secret key and directs to settings.secretSet; the UI renders configured/not-configured with Replace and Clear rather than an input.

Two worker fixes were rejected and redone: unchecked type assertions had been silenced with 'x, _ := desc.(*settings.Bool)', which relocates the panic into Registry.SetBool (it dereferences b.key with no nil check) instead of removing it — each site now checks ok and returns a self-diagnosing -32603; and the screen stringified unknown values, so a malformed value rendered as literal '[object Object]' into a field the user could save back — values are now narrowed per control kind with a logged fallback.

Remaining OSC 52 work is tracked on nocx-3cc, not silently carried here.

title: EDITOR-W2: keymap at highest precedence
description:
Spec W2. Bind Enter (submit), Shift-Enter (newline), Escape (clear draft without interrupting), Ctrl-C (copy if a selection exists, else clear + actions.cancel()) inside Prec.highest(keymap.of([...])).

CM6's defaultKeymap binds Enter and Escape. Without explicit precedence, Enter inserts a newline and Ctrl-C stops interrupting the shell — a silent regression in the two most-used keys at a prompt.

Handlers must ignore events fired during IME composition.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests assert each binding's decision including the Ctrl-C selection branch. An e2e asserts one submit produces exactly one block. Composition events do not trigger submit, clear or cancel.

title: EDITOR-W0: CM6 de-risk spike (throwaway)
description:
Spec .internal/specs/2026-07-25-editor-core-codemirror6-design.md, W0. Mount a bare CM6 view in the editor slot behind a flag and exercise, in this order: focus interplay with xterm and the focus-bounce (tabs.ts:407-417, :432-467); keymap precedence for Enter/Escape/Ctrl-C; IME composition; copy-on-select; auto-grow; document.elementFromPoint over the editor card.

The ownership machine is entirely focus-based while CM6 manages focus itself — this is the one seam where a surprise changes HOW we migrate, and it is cheapest to find on day one.

Test the real host: the shipping runtime is WKWebView (AD-3) and Playwright drives Chromium, which cannot establish WKWebView IME or focus behaviour. Reproduce on the actual WebView or record as unverified.

One decision only: can a CM6 adapter preserve the current single-target contract? Spike code is deleted, not merged.
acceptance_criteria: A written findings note on nocx-2gf listing every surprise, and that one decision answered. IME and focus findings either reproduced on WKWebView or explicitly marked unverified. Spike code deleted.
close_reason: Removed on owner's call: a throwaway spike duplicates W1's work and decides nothing that is not already decided. Its six verification items became acceptance criteria on EDITOR-W1 (nocx-5ns).

title: STORE-2: DocumentStore capability (atomic JSON + per-module schema version)
description:
ADR-0011. Bounded, human-recoverable configuration as atomic JSON documents — settings, profiles, groups, credential metadata, tab restore. Extract the mechanism currently private inside profile.JSONStore (temp file + rename, 0700 dir, 0600 file) into a capability others use.

Schema versions are PER MODULE, not app-wide: a single version would couple unrelated releases of settings, profiles, conversations and history, and JSON-document migrations have different transactional properties from SQLite ones. Share the migration protocol, not the version.

Note rename-over-path is the same class as nocx-ab4 (atomic write replacing a symlinked target with a regular file) — verify the target cannot be a symlink the user cares about. Also: the rename is not followed by a directory fsync, so 'atomic' is not fully crash-durable today.
acceptance_criteria: Documents are written atomically with correct permissions. Each module declares and migrates its own schema version through a shared protocol. profile.JSONStore uses the capability rather than its own implementation.
close_reason: STORE-2 landed: storage.DocumentStore (Read/Write) owns path, permissions and atomicity; profile.JSONStore uses it and no longer carries its own temp-plus-rename. Both defects the bead recorded are fixed with dedicated tests: the rename is now followed by a directory fsync (TestDocumentStore_DirFsync), and a write refuses a symlinked target rather than replacing it with a regular file (TestDocumentStore_SymlinkRefusal, the nocx-ab4 class). Schema versions are per module through a shared protocol — each module declares its own monotonic version and ordered migrations, DocumentStore stays format-agnostic — with 7 tests including multi-step, non-monotonic and missing-migration cases. The ProfileStore interface was deliberately left intact; splitting it is STORE-4. app.go wiring was unverifiable while STORE-3 was in flight and has now been confirmed: full build clean, go test -race ./... green.

title: STORE-3: SecretStore capability + the Secret type as the boundary
description:
ADR-0011. Authenticators only, in the OS keychain — never a file we write. Domain records carry an opaque SecretID; the secret behind it is reachable only through SecretStore, backend-side.

Overlaps PR11-T7, which introduces the Secret type for VaultSecret. This bead generalises it into a capability with stable SecretID references, which is what PR11-T6 needs to delete the right secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Secrets are addressed by stable SecretID. No API outside internal/credential and internal/ssh can obtain plaintext. A secret cannot be marshalled or logged.
close_reason:
STORE-3 landed: credential.SecretStore (Get/Set/Delete/Exists) addressed by opaque, stable SecretID, backed by the OS keychain. HashKey, KeyHash and the Identity{User: credentialID} convention are deleted outright — grep confirms zero non-test references. profile.Credential now carries SecretID and PassphraseSecretID as opaque strings; resolver, transport and ssh were rewired onto them. Greenfield per owner decision: no migration of existing keychain entries, no dual-read.

Verified rather than taken on report: 'go build ./...' clean; 'go test -race ./...' green across all 16 packages; no SecretID appears anywhere in frontend/ (zero frontend changes, as designed — the wire API stays credentialId-keyed); and every Secret->string conversion in the tree sits inside internal/credential (the vault encryption callback and the keyring handoff) or internal/ssh/ssh_auth.go:124 (the auth-method handoff), which is exactly the boundary ADR-0011 §2 permits.

title: EDITOR-W7: ADR-0010 — CodeMirror 6 as the editor core (runs before implementation)
description:
Spec W7, ordered FIRST among the code tasks. ADR-0004 section 3 is accepted and says avoid contenteditable; writing W1-W5 against it and documenting afterwards means every intermediate commit contradicts an adopted decision with nothing authorizing the change. AGENTS.md: if an AD is wrong, change it deliberately rather than routing around it.

Record: the contenteditable ban targeted the HAND-ROLLED variant and stays in force for it — CM6 is the mitigation for the very IME, undo and selection problems that motivated the ban. Record the measured bundle cost (321 KB raw / 102 KB gzip, reproduction command in the spec), the two admitted behaviour changes (wrapped lines now grow the box; undo moves from native to CM6 history), and that per-target decoration ownership is deferred to nocx-w7h.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-0010 merged and ADR-0004 section 3 annotated as revised, so a future reader cannot follow the old sentence into a hand-rolled overlay.

title: STORE-1: shared storage path resolution (config / data / cache dirs)
description:
ADR-0011. One component resolves where things live, distinguishing OS roles: configuration documents in the config dir, content.db in the application-data dir, disposable indexes in the cache dir, secrets in the keychain. On macOS these may resolve under the same Application Support tree; on Linux the XDG distinction is real.

Removes the os.TempDir() fallback at internal/app/app.go:66, which writes profiles to the fixed shared path /tmp/nocx-profiles.json.
acceptance_criteria: A single injected component returns the four locations per platform. No store computes its own path. The /tmp fallback is gone; failure to resolve a location is an explicit error, not a silent fallback.
close_reason: STORE-1 landed: internal/storage.Paths + NewOSPaths(appName) resolving config/data/cache per OS role, no fallback — an unresolvable role is an explicit error. internal/app/app.go now constructs it at the composition root and propagates the error out of New(); the os.UserConfigDir warn-and-continue branch, the configDir=='' branch and the os.TempDir() fallback that wrote profiles to the shared /tmp/nocx-profiles.json are deleted (grep confirms zero matches in internal/app). profile.NewJSONStore receives paths.ConfigDir()/profiles.json. Tests: 5 Linux subtests covering XDG overrides, XDG-unset defaults, and the HOME-unset error path; macOS subtests skip off-platform.

title: PR11-T10: replace the vault's unauthenticated AES-CBC with an AEAD
description:
internal/credential/vault.go:97-114 persists bare AES-CBC with no MAC, and :274-295 accepts padding after checking only the final length byte. Modified ciphertext can decrypt successfully into altered plaintext — malleable, unauthenticated encryption.

Use an AEAD with versioned parameters so the format can be migrated later. Note the vault is the non-keychain path; PR11-T7 changes the type it stores but deliberately does not touch this.
acceptance_criteria: Ciphertext is authenticated; a single flipped bit in a stored blob fails decryption with a clear error rather than yielding altered plaintext. Parameters carry a version. Existing stored secrets migrate or are re-prompted, decided and recorded.
close_reason: AES-256-GCM replaces the unauthenticated AES-CBC in 2f30116. Format v2 is versioned, AAD binds version/salt/iterations/key length, nonce and salt are fresh per Marshal from crypto/rand, v1 vaults are refused explicitly, and auth failure is indistinguishable from a wrong passphrase. Five tamper tests (ciphertext byte, tag byte, version field, old-format refusal, wrong-password indistinguishability) — verified they fail on the shape of code being replaced, which a round-trip test would not. KDF deliberately untouched, split out as nocx-dcd.

title: PR11-T6: deleting a credential deletes its secrets
description:
Plan v3 Task 6. internal/transport/ws.go:998-1010 deletes metadata only; the keychain entry is orphaned permanently.

Needs T4 first because the reference model must be stable: password saves by credential ID key on Identity{User: credentialID} while key passphrases key on KeyHash, and metadata stores only KeyPath — so once metadata is gone there is no hash left to derive. Load the metadata BEFORE deleting it, derive both keys, then delete metadata first and secrets after (ADR-0011 section 4: a brief unreachable orphan beats metadata pointing at a deleted secret).

INTERIM IMPLEMENTATION LANDED in b9b0485 — deliberately left open, and the remaining dependency is real rather than bookkeeping.

What shipped: credentials.delete derives both secret keys before removing metadata (a passphrase keys on HashKey of the key material while metadata holds only KeyPath, so metadata-first would strand it forever), then deletes metadata and both secrets best-effort with errors.Join, per ADR-0011 §4 — a brief unreachable orphan beats a dangling reference. A missing key file returns an error rather than skipping silently. Four tests, the passphrase one confirmed to fail on the naive implementation.

Why this stays open: it is blocked by nocx-r60 (STORE-3), and that bead says why — it generalises the Secret type into a capability with stable SecretID references, 'which is what PR11-T6 needs to delete the right secrets'. The shipped version derives keys ad hoc: the password from the credential ID, the passphrase by re-reading the private key file and hashing it. That works, but it is exactly the fragility STORE-3 removes, and it is the direct cause of nocx-dm0 — with a stable SecretID there would be nothing to re-derive from a file the user may already have deleted.

So the merge ships a working delete cascade, not the final one. Close this when STORE-3 lands and the cascade is rewritten against SecretID.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting a credential removes metadata, password entry and key-passphrase entry. Secret-deletion failure is reported while metadata deletion stands. Test uses keyring.MockInit() and the real ID assigned by the create RPC, never a hardcoded ID format.
close_reason: Closed by STORE-3 (nocx-r60), which is the condition this bead recorded for closure: the cascade is rewritten against stable SecretIDs. It no longer re-reads and re-hashes the private key file to find the passphrase secret — it reads both SecretIDs off the credential metadata, deletes metadata first, then deletes both secrets best-effort with errors.Join (ADR-0011 §4 order). TestDeleteCascade_KeyFileDeleted covers the case that motivated the rewrite: deletion still removes the passphrase when the user has already deleted the key file. Note nocx-dm0 stays OPEN — the cascade remains best-effort by design and still has no janitor for orphans; SecretID removed the re-derivation fragility, not that gap.

title: PR11-T7: VaultSecret stops being serializable (Secret type)
description:
Plan v3 Task 7. internal/credential/credential.go:59-64 defines Value string `json:"value"` — a secret designed to marshal.

Add internal/credential/secret.go: a Secret that refuses MarshalJSON/MarshalText, renders [REDACTED] through String/GoString/LogValue, and exposes plaintext only via Use(func([]byte) error). Migrate VaultSecret to it.

SCOPE HONESTLY: this touches encryption and decryption DTOs, their adapters, and existing credential tests — more than three files. It does NOT fix the vault's unauthenticated AES-CBC or its length-only padding check (vault.go:97-114, :274-295); that is a separate bead. Do not mistake this for the crypto fix.

After T4 the boundary is that no API returns a secret outward; this type is what keeps an accident inside internal/credential or internal/ssh from undoing that.
acceptance_criteria: json.Marshal of a struct containing a Secret returns an error. fmt %v/%s/%#v and slog all render [REDACTED]. The vault still round-trips a stored secret through save and load.
close_reason:
Landed in a90e31e. Secret refuses MarshalJSON AND MarshalText (encoding/json falls back to the latter, so only one would leave the hole open), renders [REDACTED] via String/GoString/Format/LogValue, and exposes plaintext only through Use(func([]byte) error). Migrated VaultSecret.Value, the CredentialStore interface, both backends and ssh_auth. json.Marshal(VaultSecret) now errors.

Vault persistence uses a private DTO that reads plaintext through Use at the encryption boundary only.

One deliberate escape, documented in the commit rather than buried: x/crypto/ssh accepts a password only as a string, so passwordCallbackFromSecret materialises it inside gossh.PasswordCallback, invoked only on an actual server challenge. Plaintext now lives for one callback instead of for the lifetime of the auth chain, which the previous string-in-authChainEntry did.

Gates: gofumpt, golangci-lint, go test -race ./... , tsc, eslint, prettier, vitest 381/381. Removals diff reviewed — nothing lost. gofumpt initially failed on two files (the worker checked gofmt, not the project's stricter gate) and was fixed before commit.

title: PR11-T8: wire the connection pool and fix client/jump lifetime
description:
Second plan, not the credential boundary. AD-4 requires a ref-counted ssh.Client pool keyed by host+identity, with the connection closing on the last referencing tab.

Today it is dead code: ConnPool.defaultDial (pool.go:174-180) returns an error and its own comment calls itself a placeholder awaiting 'the real wiring'. Production dials directly at ssh_real.go:69-77 and appends every client to rc.clients (:75-77); channel close (ssh_channel.go:33-38) closes only the session, so clients close only in global RealClient.Close, which normal tab closure never reaches. Jump clients leak independently (ssh_dial.go:99-103). Acquire/Release are referenced only by pool tests — the tests exercise an implementation nothing calls.

Also: the pool key is host/user/port only (pool.go:16-22), so different identities or jump routes would incorrectly share authentication; Release has no per-handle once guard (:134-153), so double-releasing one of two handles closes the connection beneath a live channel.
acceptance_criteria: Production dials through the pool. Key includes identity and jump route, not just host/user/port. Closing the last tab referencing a connection closes it, including the jump transport. Double release cannot close a connection with a live channel. Covered by race tests.
close_reason: Landed in 9d411ec. Production dials through the pool via AcquireDial; poolKey carries credential identity and resolved jump route (the authorization fix — the old host/user/port key would have shared one authenticated connection across principals); Release is idempotent per handle via sync.Once; the bastion is acquired from the same pool so it is ref-counted and closes with the last target through it; channel close releases the pool ref. Eight race tests. Three (DoubleReleaseCannotCloseLiveChannel, DoubleReleaseIsIdempotentPerHandle, ConcurrentDoubleRelease) verified load-bearing by mutation — neutering the sync.Once makes all three fail. Waiter cancellation was a stated compromise, scoped to and delivered by nocx-e4g.

title: Authoritative command output capture: output is DOM-only today, so nothing can consume it as data
description:
Command output exists only as rendered DOM. BlockRecord (frontend/src/scrollback/blocks.ts:32-45)
holds `el: HTMLElement` and no text; the content is spans that serializer.ts reconstructed from
xterm cells with a hardcoded Tokyo Night palette. CommandRecord (command-ledger.ts:12-25) holds
metadata only — command, cwd, host, status, exitCode, startedAt/endedAt, trusted — which is the
right metadata and is genuinely ready.

So anything that needs the OUTPUT has to scrape el.textContent: it couples the consumer to
presentation markup, flattens all structure, and reads a re-render rather than an authoritative
capture.

It is also already lossy. Per nocx-4ff.26 the xterm scrollback caps at 10k lines and the block is
serialized at marker D, so longer output has lost its beginning before we ever look. A human
notices they are staring at a tail; an agent will reason confidently about a fragment.

FOUR CONSUMERS, ONE MISSING PRIMITIVE:
- nocx-dw3   agent context ("context from current work")
- nocx-4ff.21 filter output in place + download as file
- nocx-4ff.26 the truncation bug itself
- the @cmd:42 / @output:42 mention idea for the agent editor

SHAPE: capture incrementally in the FRONTEND, between the C and D markers, as bytes arrive —
not by reading the xterm buffer at D. The frontend already receives every byte and already knows
the marker boundaries. The backend cannot do it: it does not parse OSC and therefore cannot see
command boundaries (AD-6). This also removes the scrollback dependency entirely, which is what
makes it a fix for nocx-4ff.26 rather than a workaround.

STORAGE: this is exactly the append-heavy, unbounded, query-oriented private content that
ADR-0011 introduces ContentDB for. It is a strong candidate to be the FIRST consumer that makes
the SQLite implementation necessary.

POLICY, not optional: captured output can contain secrets (a printed token, a config dump).
Retention, redaction and what may be sent to a remote model all need an answer before agent mode
consumes it — relates nocx-23v.
notes:
CORRECTION (owner, 2026-07-25): content must live on the BACKEND. My earlier note said capture belongs in the frontend because only the frontend parses OSC 133 and knows command boundaries. That reasoning was about SEMANTICS, and I wrongly extended it to STORAGE.

Frontend-only capture cannot deliver the two things it exists for: history does not survive a restart or a reconnect, and an agent running backend-side would have to pull content back through the renderer.

RESOLUTION, and it does not bend AD-6: capture is not sniffing. The frontend parses OSC 133 and tells the backend the BOUNDARIES — command N spans byte offsets X..Y. The backend stores the byte range it was told about and never interprets it. Frontend owns semantics, backend owns storage, neither owns both.

This fits machinery that already exists: AD-9 gives the backend a bounded per-session output ring keyed by a monotonic byte offset, and the frontend already acks offsets. The capture path extends that from a replay buffer into durable content (ADR-0011 ContentDB), rather than inventing a parallel mechanism.

SECURITY ARGUMENT, which is now decisive: after nocx-<xss bead> the renderer must be treated as injectable. Command output can carry secrets. If content is captured and stored backend-side and the agent also runs backend-side (nocx-dw3 drives pi over RPC from Go), then output never transits the injectable layer on its way to the model. Frontend-side content would force exactly that transit.

Consequence: this bead is very likely the first real consumer of ContentDB, which is what turns the SQLite seam in ADR-0011 into an implementation.

title: PR #11 persists profiles in its own JSON store, bypassing internal/config
description:
PR #11 (feat/ssh-connection-manager, +8025/-605, 52 files) adds internal/profile/store.go
— a JSONStore that writes its own file: os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700), json.MarshalIndent,
temp file + rename. It has zero references to internal/config.

In the same PR, internal/config/config.go is STILL the no-op Stub (Load/Save log and
return nil). So the branch ships a working persistence layer beside a config module that
by design cannot persist anything.

The implementation is not sloppy — the atomic temp+rename and 0700 dir are better than
what config has. That is what makes it a problem: it is a well-built silo, the next
feature will copy it, and by then "settings live in two places" is the architecture.

Owner requirement (2026-07-25): settings are declared in a registry from which the
settings screen is GENERATED (nocx-1ei), persisted through config (nocx-jap). SSH
profiles are user-facing settings and belong in that path.

Cheapest reversible fix, and the recommendation: do not block the PR on the registry
existing. Keep JSONStore, but make it an injected implementation chosen at the single
composition root per AD-8, so replacing it with registry-backed storage later is a
one-line change at the root instead of a rewrite of every call site.

Also check: rename-over-path is the same class as nocx-ab4 (writeFileAtomic replacing a
symlinked target with a regular file). Verify the profile path cannot be a symlink the
user cares about.
notes:
SUPERSEDED TWICE (2026-07-25). First version of this bead said 'wrap JSONStore behind config'. Wrong: profiles are not settings. Settings are a flat, enumerable set of declared knobs from which a screen is GENERATED (nocx-1ei); profiles are a CRUD collection with IDs, grouping and credential links. Pushing them through config's Get(key)/Set(key any) bag would be worse — that untyped bag is the weak design nocx-1ei exists to replace.

Second version said 'extract one shared persistence primitive'. Also too narrow — one atomic-file-write primitive does not serve a keychain or SQLite.

CURRENT DIRECTION (owner, 2026-07-25): separate ENTITIES from the STORAGE LAYER. Each entity declares a typed repository interface; backends are swappable implementations; the pairing is chosen at the single composition root (AD-8 applied to persistence).

  Settings -> JSON | Profiles -> JSON | Credentials -> vault/keychain
  Conversations -> SQLite | History -> SQLite

Refinement that matters most: the boundary runs by FIELD SENSITIVITY, not by entity. One SSH profile spans two backends — host/user/port/group to JSON, password and key passphrase to the vault. That split must be expressed in the TYPE, not remembered. PR #11 already makes this split informally (profile.Credential metadata vs internal/credential secrets), and its being informal is plausibly why the password reached a log line at frontend/src/tabs.ts:560.

Genuinely shared and small: config-dir/path resolution, schema version + migration protocol, sensitivity classification.

CREDIT: PR #11's SHAPE is already right — ProfileStore interface, JSONStore implementation, wiring in internal/app/app.go (the composition root). Missing: shared path resolution (hence the os.TempDir() fallback at app.go:66), schema versioning, and the sensitivity rule.

CONSEQUENCE TO DECIDE: SQLite is not in the stack, and architecture.md:180 says 'plain files in the OS config dir' with format still an open ASSUMPTION at :198. AI conversations in SQLite revises that — needs an ADR, not a silent dependency.

Codex asked to critique this shape; answer pending.
close_reason: Resolved by the ADR-0011 epic (nocx-6ek). The silo is gone: profile.JSONStore no longer writes its own file — it goes through storage.DocumentStore, which owns the 0700 dir, the 0600 file, the temp-plus-rename, and now also the directory fsync and a symlink-target refusal that the private version lacked. internal/config is deleted outright rather than left as a second answer, and settings now come from a typed registry (nocx-1ei) persisted through the same DocumentStore. 'Settings live in two places' did not become the architecture.

title: [bug] Prompt-cycle state is reduced in three places that must agree by hand
description:
The A/B/C/D marker cycle is independently re-derived by three owners:
- frontend/src/input-state.ts:14 — InputStateController: state / trusted / owned
- frontend/src/command-ledger.ts:34 — CycleState: sawCleanA / sawB / running, whose own
  comment says its trust logic "mirrors" the state machine
- frontend/src/scrollback/blocks.ts:440 — BlockManager: a second running record with its
  own clock, status and exit-code lifecycle
plus Tab itself holding _pendingCommand and _lastExitCode (tabs.ts:97).

"Mirrors" is the exact word AD-6 exists to catch: two owners of one truth, kept in sync
by hand until they drift. They already disagree semantically — the ledger models
`interrupted` and `unknown` and tracks marker disposal (command-ledger.ts:10), while
BlockRecord knows only running/success/failure and its unsafe finalizer labels an
abandoned block a failure with no exit code (blocks.ts:604).

Shape of the fix: one reducer emits semantic prompt/command lifecycle events; the ledger
and the block presentation become projections of it rather than parallel derivations.

Found by the codex architecture review of nocx-2gf. Independent of the CM6 migration —
but the migration is a good moment, because a swap that "changes nothing" also preserves
this.

title: [bug] ShellInputTarget hand-rolls bracketed paste, contradicting its own comment and the recorded lesson
description:
frontend/src/input-target.ts:33-34 defines PASTE_START/PASTE_END and :42 sends
`${PASTE_START}${doc}${PASTE_END}\r` down sendRaw. That is exactly the hand-rolled
wrapper that memory `lesson-nocx-input-editor-do-not-hand-roll` says must not exist:
"do NOT hand-roll bracketed-paste wrappers when submitting the DOM editor's command.
Route through the terminal engine's term.paste(text) which wraps ONLY when the shell
enabled mode 2004. Hardcoded wrappers leaked as literal 00~/01~ into the command when
2004 wasn't (yet) enabled — e.g. a fast second submit racing the prompt."

The code even documents the leak as accepted (input-target.ts:30-32): "When mode IS off
the wrappers leak but the shell interprets \n as accept-line, which also executes every
line. Either way, the user gets the entire composed command."

And tabs.ts:295-296 claims the opposite of what the code does: "paste() delegates
bracketed-paste wrapping to the engine (correct for mode 2004); sendRaw carries the CR."
ShellInputTarget has no paste() and never touches the engine.

So three sources disagree: the lesson says route through term.paste(), tabs.ts says we
already do, and input-target.ts hand-rolls and calls the leak acceptable. At most one is
right. Resolve which, then make code and comments agree.

Note nocx-4ff.14 is cited in the comment for the multi-line rationale — whatever the fix,
a multi-line composition must still execute every line.
Found during the codex review of the editor-core spec (nocx-2gf).
notes:
WHY THIS IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY, NOT HYGIENE (owner insight, 2026-07-25): the danger of multi-line input is not the multi-line-ness — it is text reaching the PTY WITHOUT passing through the editor.

Tabby warns with a modal on multi-line paste because it has no editor of its own: paste goes straight to the terminal, so a dialog is the only intervention point. Owner's experience: it nags constantly and the answer is a blind yes/no.

We are structurally better placed. In enhanced mode a paste lands in the DOM editor: visible, editable, caret in it, nothing runs until Enter. The user reads what they are about to execute instead of approving it blind. No modal needed — and we should NOT add one.

That advantage exists only while the submit path is correct. With the hand-rolled wrappers, when mode 2004 is off the leak turns every newline into accept-line (input-target.ts:30-32 says so outright), and the lines execute as they arrive — bypassing the very review the editor exists to provide.

So the promise to make, and to test:
- ENHANCED mode: pasted or injected text is composed, never executed, until an explicit submit. Safe by construction.
- RAW mode (running command, alt-screen, unintegrated shell): paste goes to the PTY and the shell decides, exactly as in any terminal. We must not intercept there — that would break fail-open and raw routing (ADR-0004 section 1).

This matters more as text stops coming only from the user: ghost text from history (nocx-4ff.23), edit-and-rerun (nocx-4ff.20), and agent-composed commands (nocx-dw3) all put non-typed text into the editor. The invariant 'composed text never self-executes' is what makes those features safe to build.

title: [epic] Warpify: shell integration on any host, at any depth
description:
Bootstrap the OSC 7 / OSC 133 shell integration into ANY shell the user lands in —
ssh, ssh through a jump host, docker exec, tmux, nix-shell — so the enhanced command
line is not a local-machine-only feature. This is AD-5 Tier A extended to arbitrary
depth. Warp calls it "warpify".

TODAY: ActivationEnv is called in exactly one place, internal/app/app.go:56 — the
LOCAL pty factory. internal/ssh/ssh_real.go has no Setenv/SendEnv at all. So an SSH
tab gets no markers, owned stays false, and the DOM editor never appears. Enhanced
input is local-only, by omission rather than by design.

MECHANISM: the bootstrap rides the SAME byte stream — we type one line into whatever
shell is at the far end. No second channel, no files left behind, and it works through
N hops by construction because we are just writing into the session that already
exists. Contrast internal/shellintegration/install_remote.go (~165 lines, SFTP): zero
call sites, zero tests, and a known bug list (world-readable perms, TOCTOU in
appendGateRemote, -l login-shell vs .bashrc gate mismatch, GetRemoteHome parsing
`echo $HOME` through the banner) — see nocx-ccn.

DESIGN SEAM (AD-8): delivery is a strategy behind one interface, not an if-chain:
  - local-env      — today's ActivationEnv at spawn
  - in-band        — the warpify bootstrap (this epic's default)
  - sftp-install   — install_remote.go, kept as an implementation, not the only path
Whether nocx-ccn is fixed or retired is decided inside this epic, not assumed.

MUST COVER:
- explicit action ("integrate this session") AND an automatic trigger; auto must not
  be a blind regex on the typed command — we own the input surface and the ledger
  knows the host, so a per-host decision is available and idempotent
- version negotiation: local script version (currently 7) vs whatever answered
- fail-open: an unintegrated or refusing shell degrades to a plain terminal, never
  to an invisible prompt (ADR-0004 section 1, ADR-0006 section 5)
- nested depth: NOCX_SESSION_ID must keep identifying WHICH shell owns input when
  several integrated shells are stacked
- the bootstrap payload is executed by the remote shell — say so plainly in the ADR

DOC BUG FOUND: docs/architecture.md:188 names the Tier-B remote HELPER BINARY
"Warpify Tier-B remote helper" and defers it. Warp's warpify is Tier A shell hooks,
which is this epic and is NOT deferred. Left uncorrected, a reader defers the wrong
thing. Fix the naming in architecture.md as part of this epic.
notes:
SECURITY CONSTRAINT (codex review, 2026-07-25): any process can print OSC sequences. If the shell integration carries structured payloads in-band (alias/function snapshots, resolution answers, agent events), a program running INSIDE the session can forge them — it only has to write bytes. Today's OSC 133 markers are low-value to forge; a metadata bus is not.

Required in the design, not bolted on: payloads bound to the session via the existing NOCX_SESSION_ID nonce, a version field, and a hard size cap so a hostile or merely broken program cannot flood or spoof the channel. Same class of problem as OSC 52 clipboard writes, which we already gate.

This also constrains the semantic epic (nocx-w7h), which consumes those payloads, and the relay (nocx-if6), where the far end is by definition less trusted.

title: [epic] Editor core on CodeMirror 6 (replaces the textarea internals)
description:
Replace the internals of CommandEditor (frontend/src/editor.ts) with CodeMirror 6,
preserving the public API so tabs.ts and the input-ownership machine are untouched.

WHY NOW: history (nocx-4ff.6), highlighting (nocx-4ff.22) and ghost-text (nocx-4ff.23)
all need the same machinery — a render layer separate from the input surface, and
character-level screen coordinates for popups and inline decorations. A <textarea>
renders one uniform colour and knows no coordinates, so building those three on it
means hand-rolling caret measurement and a popup, then throwing that away. Blast
radius is at its lifetime minimum: one consumer (tabs.ts, 13 call sites) and the
InputTarget interface already declares complete?() and history?() with no impl.

MEASURED: CM6 (state+view+autocomplete+commands+legacy shell mode) = 321 KB raw /
102 KB gzip, vs xterm.js 289 KB / 65 KB. Non-issue for a desktop bundle.

BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING BY CONTRACT: no new user-facing features land in this epic.
Done = every existing vitest + e2e green and the editor looks and behaves identically.
Features come after, in the semantic epic.

INVARIANTS THAT MUST SURVIVE (all three already cost us a session):
- submit routes through term.paste(), never hand-rolled ESC[200~ wrappers
  (memory: lesson-nocx-input-editor-do-not-hand-roll)
- atomic handoff order: hide -> clear -> send (ADR-0004 section 2)
- .nocx-editor { z-index: 20 } or .xterm-link-layer wins hit-testing again (nocx-4ff.16)

KNOWN COSTS / RISKS:
- focus interplay: the whole ownership machine is focus-based, CM6 manages focus
  itself. Top risk; verify first.
- keymap precedence: our Enter / Escape / Ctrl-C must be Prec.highest or CM6's
  defaultKeymap wins and Ctrl-C stops interrupting.
- jsdom has no layout, so CM6 view behaviour is not testable there -> forces the
  vitest-browser-mode decision (nocx-foz).
- e2e/command-editor.spec.ts asserts elementFromPoint == TEXTAREA; will be rewritten.
- IME: zero test coverage today; the document-level keydown redirect (tabs.ts:432)
  can destroy composition state. Pre-existing hole this epic must close.
- tabs.ts:480-491 copy-on-select reads .textarea directly; replaced by a narrow
  selection accessor.

ADR REQUIRED: ADR-0010 revises ADR-0004 section 3 ("avoid contenteditable"). That
ban targeted HAND-ROLLED contenteditable; CM6 is the mitigation for exactly the
IME/undo problems behind it. The ban stays in force for the hand-rolled variant.
notes:
AI/agent requirement (owner, 2026-07-25): the new editor must later host AI dialogs and pull context from current work; Pi (pi.dev) is the intended agent.

Already designed for: ADR-0004 section 3 defines InputTarget with ShellInputTarget + AgentInputTarget on the SAME editor, separate drafts/histories, explicit mode switch (never a magic '?' prefix). Bead nocx-4ff.7 exists. vision.md:75 Phase 3 = 'natural-language query to any AI model the user chooses, bring-your-own, including fully local'.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS EPIC: decoration/language set must be a property of the ACTIVE TARGET, not global — shell mode colours shell syntax, agent mode renders prose plus mentions of blocks/files. A textarea cannot do per-target inline mentions at all; this strengthens the CM6 choice. Context source is the command-ledger (cwd, host, exit code, duration) plus DOM blocks — needs a read interface defined at this boundary.

OPEN FORK (blocks nocx-4ff.7, not this epic): Pi evidence from /home/dev/repos/orca — src/main/pi/ + src/shared/pi-agent-kind.ts show Pi is launched as a TUI command (detected via command-token scan) and extended through the PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR env contract + an extension API that reports agent_end milestone events back to the host. A TUI agent puts the session in ALT_SCREEN, where our input-ownership machine hands the full viewport to the app and the DOM editor is gone by design — i.e. agent-as-TUI bypasses our editor entirely. Owning the input surface requires Pi in a programmatic/headless mode instead. Unresolved: whether Pi offers one.
Design spec: .internal/specs/2026-07-25-editor-core-codemirror6-design.md (W0 spike -> W1 swap -> W2 keymap -> W3 selection seam -> W4 insertText/focus-bounce -> W6 target extension seam -> W5 tests -> W7 ADR-0010)
CORRECTION (codex review, 2026-07-25): the epic description above says 'the InputTarget interface already declares complete?() and history?() with no impl'. That is WRONG. frontend/src/input-target.ts:9-13 declares only id, label, submit. ADR-0004 section 3 describes the richer interface; the implementation never followed. Same error was repeated in nocx-w7h and nocx-dw3 — the 'seam already exists' argument does not hold for any of them.

Consequence: the per-target editorExtensions() seam was REMOVED from this epic (was W6) and moved to nocx-w7h, which is the first real consumer. tabs.ts does not use InputTargetRegistry at all (constructs ShellInputTarget directly at :297) and the registry has no change notification, so wiring it here would have smuggled a second epic into a behaviour-preserving one.

Defects discovered by the same review, filed separately: nocx-hi2 (ShellInputTarget hand-rolls bracketed paste, contradicting both the recorded lesson and tabs.ts's own comment — P1, resolve before W1), nocx-0oc (.nocx-editor has no z-index though three comments claim 20), nocx-m7x (e2e clicks .nocx-editor-submit, removed in 7204aff — already failing).

Also confirmed: renderers/wterm.ts:114 setReadOnly is a documented no-op, so under wterm the prompt has no read-only guard at all and input ownership rests on focus alone. Pre-existing, but it makes any 'wterm parity' claim unverifiable until W0 establishes what actually stops wterm from forwarding keystrokes.

title: Beads sync is one-way: nothing pulls the Dolt data, so a teammate's backlog is only as fresh as their last manual bd dolt pull
description:
Three people, three machines, one shared Dolt remote (refs/dolt/data on the git origin). Today .githooks/pre-push runs bd dolt push, so state LEAVES each machine on git push — and nothing ever brings it back. core.hooksPath points at .githooks/, so the beads shims in .beads/hooks/ (post-merge, post-checkout — the ones that would sync on the way in) never execute. A colleague sees your closed bead only when they remember 'bd dolt pull' by hand.

Cadence was set deliberately in nocx-lte ('on git push, not per-commit or per-bd-mutation'); this bead does not revise that for the write side, it adds the missing read side.

RESEARCH (2026-07-25, upstream docs + DoltHub blog):
• Our topology is beads' documented workflow #2, 'Multiple Agents, Multiple Clones, Single Shared Remote'. Supported, with a named cost: pull before push when the remote has advanced, and one agent's push blocks the others until they pull.
• dolt.auto-push EXISTS and is opt-in-off by design, interval 5m, timeout 30s. It stays off here: upstream warns that concurrent pushes to a GIT-PROTOCOL Dolt remote can corrupt or strand remote history when writers race — which is exactly three people pushing on claim.
• A claim is therefore NOT a lock and no sync cadence makes it one. Hash IDs prevent ID collisions, not double-claims: both writers push, Dolt merges, last write wins. Real exclusion would need bd merge-slot or a shared Dolt sql-server instead of git refs.
• Escape hatch if claim races ever get frequent: move off the git protocol to a hosted/self-hosted Dolt sql-server; beads routes credentials per protocol type (git vs external Dolt server). Not now — it trades a rare problem for a server to run.

WORK
1. .githooks/post-merge + post-checkout calling a new pull_beads_state() in .githooks/beads-hook.sh, so git pull refreshes the tracker. Failure policy MUST be softer than the push side: a failed pull warns and lets the checkout stand — blocking someone's git pull over a stale backlog is worse than the staleness.
2. AGENTS.md claim protocol: bd dolt pull && bd update <id> --claim && bd dolt push. Pull first shrinks the race window, push after publishes the claim immediately, without turning on blind auto-push.
3. Re-test 'bd hooks run <hook>' on bd 1.1.0. nocx-lte measured 1.0.5 and found the shims silent no-ops, which is why beads-hook.sh calls 'bd dolt push' directly; the bead explicitly asks for this re-test on upgrade. If the shims work now, prefer them.
acceptance_criteria:
• git pull / git checkout refreshes the local Dolt data without anyone typing bd dolt pull.
• A failed or impossible pull (no bd, no database, remote unreachable) never blocks git — it warns and continues.
• The claim protocol is written down where the agents actually read it (AGENTS.md).
• The bd 1.1.0 shim re-test is recorded in this bead: either the hooks now call the shim, or the note says it is still a no-op.
close_reason:
Shipped. Read side now exists: .githooks/post-merge and .githooks/post-rewrite call a new pull_beads_state() in .githooks/beads-hook.sh, so git pull refreshes the tracker without anyone typing bd dolt pull.

MEASURED, not assumed (git 2.55.0, scratch repo, three cases):
• git pull (fast-forward) -> post-merge fires.
• git pull --rebase with NO local commits -> still a fast-forward, post-merge fires.
• git pull --rebase WITH local commits -> post-merge does NOT fire; post-checkout (flag=1) and post-rewrite (arg=rebase) do.
Hence two hooks, not one. post-rewrite gates on $1=rebase so git commit --amend pays nothing (measured 0.002s vs 1.575s for a real pull).

NO post-checkout hook, deliberately: it fires on every branch switch and a network round trip there is the tax people disable hooks to escape. post-rewrite already covers the only case post-merge misses.

Failure policy is the INVERSE of the push side and that is the point: every branch returns 0. A failed push means your state never left the machine while everything looks fine locally — worth blocking for. A failed pull means you keep the backlog you already had, and blocking someone's merge over that is worse than the staleness. Timeout is 60s (BEADS_PULL_TIMEOUT) rather than the push side's 300s, because this one sits in front of an interactive command.

bd 1.1.0 SHIM RE-TEST (the open question nocx-lte left): both shims still refuse to move data. 'bd hooks run post-merge' prints 'skipping JSONL import because sync.remote is configured' and performs no Dolt pull at all. 'bd hooks run pre-push' is still the silent no-op measured on 1.0.5 — refs/dolt/data unmoved (c93f08d5 before and after). So beads-hook.sh keeps calling bd dolt push/pull directly. Re-test again on the next upgrade.

TESTS: scripts/test-beads-pull-hook.sh, 10 assertions over both hooks with a stub bd — success silent, exit 3 silent, bd absent silent, genuine failure warns + returns 0, hang hits the timeout + returns 0, amend does not invoke bd, rebase does, missing arg inert. All green. Runs from any cwd.

DOCS: AGENTS.md gained the three-step claim protocol (pull, claim, push) plus the honest caveat that a claim is not a lock and why dolt.auto-push stays off; README documents both new hooks and the test. The claim protocol went OUTSIDE the generated beads blocks so 'bd setup codex' cannot clobber it.

RESEARCH RECORD: our topology is upstream's documented workflow #2 (multiple clones, one shared remote) — supported, with pull-before-push as the named cost. dolt.auto-push exists, is opt-in-off, 5m interval; upstream warns concurrent pushes to a git-protocol Dolt remote can corrupt or strand remote history, which is exactly three people pushing on claim. Escape hatch if races become routine: shared Dolt sql-server instead of git refs.

title: Epic: Command input & blocks (input-ownership state machine)
description:
Warp-style command experience per ADR-0004. The command being composed is freely-editable DOM text (a real editor), decoupled from PTY line discipline; the same surface later hosts LLM agent input. Two orthogonal axes: (1) an input-ownership state machine (RAW / PROMPT_READY / ALT_SCREEN) where nocx owns input ONLY at a positively-identified integrated shell prompt and everything else routes raw to the PTY; (2) the editor as a passive surface behind a pluggable InputTarget registry (ShellInputTarget first, AgentInputTarget later). Prompt/echo handled by marker-only prompt + atomic handoff (hide editor -> bracketed-paste + CR), no stty / no readline mirroring. Output stays in one continuous xterm with OSC-133 decorations; freeze-to-DOM is deferred. See docs/decisions/0004-input-ownership-and-editor-abstraction.md.

## Success Criteria

A freely-editable DOM command-input block appears at a clean local zsh/bash prompt,
hands off atomically to the PTY on Enter (bracketed paste + CR, command painted once),
and fails open to a normal terminal everywhere else (unintegrated shell, nested/SSH,
running command, alt-screen, PS2). The user is never trapped in an invisible prompt:
readiness gating (nocx-4ff.10) and a state-independent native-mode escape (nocx-4ff.9)
are in place before ENHANCED_INPUT is enabled by default. Plan:
.internal/plans/2026-07-24-warp-editable-command-input.md

title: OSC 52: programs cannot reach the clipboard — xterm.js drops the sequence
description:
xterm.js registers OSC handlers for 0,1,2,4,8,10,11,12,104,110,111,112 and silently discards everything else, so OSC 52 never arrives. Any program that copies on the user's behalf therefore reaches nothing, with no error: Claude Code (verified in binary 2.1.217 — ']52;c;' with a tmux branch, plus pbcopy/xclip/xsel/wl-copy fallbacks), tmux, vim with clipboard=unnamed, and everything over SSH where OSC 52 is the only route to a local clipboard at all. This is a silent regression against every terminal the user already runs.

Fix through parser.registerOscHandler(52, ...) — the same mechanism already carrying OSC 7 in frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts:188. registerOscHandler accepts arbitrary identifiers, so no engine patch is needed.

Do NOT copy Tabby's approach (tabby-terminal/src/middleware/oscProcessing.ts): it re-parses the byte stream ahead of the engine, which duplicates VT parsing that AD-6 assigns to the VT frontend, and at line 57 it buffers the remainder without bound or timeout when no terminator arrives — a stream carrying an unterminated sequence stalls output while accumulating memory. Registering on the engine's parser inherits chunk reassembly and both terminator forms for free; the engine also already caps an OSC payload at 1e7 chars.

Write only. The read form (]52;c;?) must have no code path, so a remote host on an SSH session cannot exfiltrate the clipboard. iTerm2, kitty and wezterm take the same stance; Tabby arrives there implicitly by honouring only targets 'c' and empty.
acceptance_criteria: printf '\033]52;c;<base64>\007' places the decoded text on the system clipboard; selecting text inside a Claude Code session running in nocx reaches the clipboard; the read form is ignored entirely.
close_reason: OSC 52 arrives through parser.registerOscHandler(52,...) beside the existing OSC 7 handler — no byte-stream middleware, so no repeat of Tabby's unbounded buffer. Writes are denied by default with a Warp-style banner carrying the remedy (allow / don't show again / dismiss); the read form has no code path at all. Decoder rejects the read form, non-clipboard targets, malformed base64, zero-byte payloads, and oversized ones before decoding. Verified by hand: printf of an OSC 52 sequence leaves the clipboard untouched after dismissing the banner. Note a local program can still reach the clipboard via pbcopy — no terminal gates that, Warp included; this protects what has no second door, i.e. content over SSH.

title: [bug] Glyph corruption on resize and after closing a tab
description:
Two reproductions of what is almost certainly one renderer defect, both reported with screenshots by the owner.
(a) Resize the window: existing glyphs turn into mangled overlapping shapes.
(b) Close the last tab, land on the neighbour, type: red garbage appears instead of characters.
25de485 made the ResizeObserver call refreshAtlas() instead of a bare clearTextureAtlas(), which was supposed to cover (a); it is evidently not enough, or the repaint happens before the new grid is in place. Note the tab-activation path also calls refreshAtlas(), which is the (b) path.
An earlier e2e attempt at this failed to discriminate because it nudged the pane by 1px on purpose to avoid a reflow — the real trigger changes the grid. A test driving page.setViewportSize() to a genuinely different cols/rows should reproduce it (see nocx-bq7).
acceptance_criteria: A real window resize and a close-tab-then-type both leave the screen rendering correctly, and an e2e test fails without the fix.
notes:
e2e pixel-test investigation (worker task_42e778c10d9f), 2026-07-22:

Engines tried:
- Playwright Chromium (headless): WebGL IS active (confirmed via canvas webgl2 context probe of the xterm renderer canvas). Pixel tests pass identically with the fix reverted — the corruption does NOT reproduce in headless Chromium. This was already known from a prior attempt.
- Playwright WebKit (headless): WebGL IS active (same confirmation method). Pixel tests ALSO pass identically with the fix reverted — the corruption does NOT reproduce in headless WebKit either.

Conclusion: no automated guard is achievable from this harness. The glyph corruption (mangled overlapping glyphs on resize, red garbage after close-tab-and-type) is specific to the real macOS WKWebView rendering context inside the Wails app. Neither Playwright engine reproduces it.

xterm.ts change (IN PLACE and UNVERIFIED against visible symptom as of handoff):
refreshAtlas() formerly called clearTextureAtlas() then term.refresh(0, rows-1). It now calls only term.refresh(0, rows-1). Rationale: clearing the texture atlas before repainting races with atlas repopulation in _updateModel. The resize path (safeFit to fit to handleResize) already refreshes the char atlas via _refreshCharAtlas(). The tab-activation path needs only a viewport refresh.

Steps 4-5 (real-app verification) are PENDING a human check:
- Resize the real WKWebView window: check for mangled overlapping glyphs
- Close a tab and type on the survivor: check for red garbage
- One tab, type: check prompt stays intact (nocx-d1f regression)

Cleanup done:
- e2e/screenshots/ deleted (leftover PNGs from prior investigation)
- /e2e/screenshots/ added to .gitignore
- No pixel test shipped (would pass in both states = false guard)

If the fix is wrong: the refreshAtlas change is the only change. To revert, restore clearTextureAtlas() calls before term.refresh().
close_reason:
Verified by the repo owner in the real WKWebView app, which is the only place this reproduces: resize no longer mangles glyphs, close-tab-then-type shows no red garbage, and nocx-d1f has not regressed (one tab, click, type renders correctly) — that last check mattered because the fix removes the clearTextureAtlas() call that 25de485 had paired with a refresh.

Fix: refreshAtlas() in frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts now only calls term.refresh(0, rows-1); the clearTextureAtlas() call is gone, because clearing before repainting races with atlas repopulation in _updateModel while the resize path already refreshes the char atlas via _refreshCharAtlas().

No automated guard ships, deliberately. Both Playwright engines were tried with the fix reverted — Chromium and WebKit, WebGL confirmed active in each — and NEITHER reproduces the corruption. A test that passes in both states is a false guard, so none was written; the finding is recorded in the notes instead. Our e2e harness is structurally blind to this class of bug.

title: Playwright webServer leaves wails dev and its vite watcher running
description: Driving 'wails dev' from Playwright's webServer does not tear down cleanly, so a run hangs for minutes after the last test and would burn a CI job's timeout. Measured: the frontend dev watcher runs in its OWN process group (vite PGID 33952, parent 'npm run dev' reparented to PPID 1) while Playwright's group is separate (33771), so neither Playwright's group kill nor a 'trap kill 0' in the webServer command can reach it. The orphan inherits the run's stdio, so with stdout/stderr piped the stream never reaches EOF; one observed run only exited after vite happened to crash with EPIPE, 3.4 minutes for 7 seconds of tests. Runs also leave 'wails dev' itself alive afterwards. Options: a globalTeardown that reaps by port and by the project-scoped vite path, or a globalSetup that starts the server under setsid and kills the whole tree.
acceptance_criteria: A full e2e run exits within seconds of the last test and leaves no wails dev, app or vite process behind.
close_reason: Fixed by gracefulShutdown: {signal: 'SIGTERM'} in playwright.config.ts. Root cause confirmed in the wails v2.13.0 source: the CLI starts the frontend watcher with Setpgid (dev_other.go:15) and reaps it from a SIGTERM handler via syscall.Kill(-pgid) (dev_other.go:32, dev.go:90/114). Playwright's default is to SIGKILL the group, so that handler never ran. Verified from a clean process table: 4 passed in 15.7s, 16.4s wall clock (was 3m26s for fewer tests), and no wails dev, app or vite process left behind.

Add an e2e spec on the existing Playwright harness at :34115 covering (a) a click on the pane hands focus to the terminal and typed characters reach it, (b) the pane render is stable across the deferred ResizeObserver run rather than being left on a cleared atlas.

Deliberately NOT landed: an e2e guard for the atlas half. title: Terminal leaked its launcher's agent session into every shell
description: nocx handed the whole parent environment to every PTY (cmd.Env = os.Environ()), so when it is started from inside a coding agent — which is how it gets developed — each shell inherited that agent's session markers. A 'claude' run in a nocx tab saw CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION and silently turned transcript saving off; the user hit this for real. The principle is general: a terminal hands out shells and must not hand out its launcher's identity with them. Fixed by scrubbing a precise list of session markers (not a CLAUDE* wildcard — stripping something like an API key would break the very tool being fixed). Related and still open: nocx does not start a LOGIN shell, so the environment is whatever nocx inherited rather than what the user's profile defines. Terminal.app runs the first shell with -l. Worth a separate look.
acceptance_criteria: A shell opened in nocx carries no launcher session markers; credentials and ordinary variables survive.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tier A shell hooks: make the shell emit OSC 133 command markers
description:
nocx-5mn.1 verified we can RECEIVE OSC 133 (ADR-0001: xterm.js returned A, B, C, D;0 and D;127 with exit codes). Nothing yet makes a shell SEND them, so every consumer of command boundaries is starved. AD-5 Tier A is exactly this: shell hooks with zero remote install, working locally and over SSH. Ship the zsh/bash hooks and inject them so a user gets this without configuring anything. Emit A at prompt start, B at prompt end, C when output starts, and D with the exit code when the command finishes.

SCOPE CORRECTION (2026-07-22): the old description claimed this unlocks the activity indicator 'driven by real command completion instead of byte heuristics (nocx-5mf)'. That is dead. nocx-5mf shipped in 2d990ee via the title-status layer (frontend/src/agent-status.ts + Tab.updateAgentStatus) and its close reason records the OSC 133 dependency as a modelling error: the two are complementary, since OSC 133 marks SHELL command boundaries and cannot see inside one long-running agent command. Do not cite nocx-5mf as justification here again — it cost a session of picking already-done work.

What genuinely remains behind these markers, and nothing else: command blocks, success/failure colouring from the D exit code, and 'a background command finished' as an explicit event rather than a byte heuristic.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a shell in nocx produces OSC 133 A/B/C/D at the right boundaries, D carries the exit code, and the frontend receives them through the registered handler.
notes: SCOPE ADDITION (2026-07-23, ADR-0004): the injected hooks must ALSO install a marker-only, visually empty prompt in enhanced mode (empty PROMPT/PS1 carrying only the OSC markers), saving and restoring the user's original prompt when integration is off or nocx exits. This is what lets the DOM input editor (nocx-4ff) own composition without a duplicate shell prompt. Raw fallback stays mandatory: if hooks/markers are absent, behave as a conventional terminal.

title: Activity indicator is always on for full-screen TUIs
description: Tabs running Claude Code or Hermes show the activity indicator permanently: those TUIs animate spinners and elapsed-time counters, so bytes never stop arriving, and any output currently counts as activity. The indicator answers 'did bytes arrive' when the user needs 'did something happen worth my attention'. Note Tabby has the identical flaw — baseTerminalTab.component.ts subscribes binaryOutput$ straight to displayActivity() — so copying it faithfully is what produced this; do not look there for the fix. Proposed rule: in the normal screen buffer any output is activity, as today; in the ALTERNATE screen buffer repaints are ignored, because a full-screen TUI redrawing itself is not news — but a bell (BEL) always counts, since that is a program explicitly asking for attention. xterm.js exposes buffer.active.type and onBell. Keep AD-6 intact: the renderer reports the facts (which buffer is active, a bell fired), the tab decides the policy — tabs.ts must not sniff bytes.
design:
How Warp does it: it does not guess from output — the SHELL tells it, via OSC 133 semantic prompt markers. A = prompt start, B = prompt end / input start, C = command output start, D;<exit> = command finished with its exit code. Ghostty, iTerm2, Kitty and WezTerm use the same substrate. 'A command finished in a background tab' is therefore an explicit event, not a heuristic, and it carries success or failure with it.

We already proved we can receive this. ADR-0001 chose xterm.js precisely because registering parser.registerOscHandler returned all five OSC 133 markers — A, B, C, D;0 and D;127 — exit codes included, where ghostty-web exposed no OSC handler registration at all. AD-5 already names OSC 133 as the Tier A substrate and epic nocx-5mn owns the shell hooks.

So the indicator should be driven by OSC 133 D, not by counting bytes: light it when a command finishes in a background tab, and it can then say more than 'something happened' — a failed command (D;non-zero) deserves a different colour from a successful one, which is what Warp shows.

Scope boundary worth stating: OSC 133 marks SHELL command boundaries. It fires when a long build ends, and when claude itself exits — but it says nothing while claude is running and wants attention mid-session, because that is inside one shell command. That case needs the program to signal: a bell, or OSC 9. Claude Code currently emits neither (see anthropics/claude-code issues #22528 and #32635, both open requests for OSC 133 support). Keep the bell rule for it and do not pretend the byte heuristic can cover it.

This makes nocx-5mf depend on the Tier A shell hooks in nocx-5mn rather than on more heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: A tab running a spinner TUI in the alternate screen stops showing a permanent activity indicator; a bell inside that TUI still lights it; ordinary shell output in the normal buffer still lights it.
notes:
How Orca does the spinning tab indicator (/Users/shady/Documents/repos/orca, src/shared/terminal-title-status.ts): detectAgentStatusFromTitle(title) classifies the TERMINAL TITLE into three states — 'working', 'idle', 'permission' — not two. Markers: Claude Code prefixes the title with ✳ when idle and with a braille spinner while working; Gemini CLI has its own symbols for all three; Pi/OMP use synthetic labels; a braille spinner anywhere in the title means working. Cursor's bare native title is explicitly excluded as carrying no status.

We can do this today with what we already have: renderer.onTitle is wired, and the user's own screenshot showed a nocx tab titled '✳ Claude Code' — the marker was arriving and we discarded it. No new protocol, no shell hooks, nothing to wait for.

'permission' is the state worth the loudest treatment: the agent is blocked on a question, which is strictly more urgent than 'finished'.

Two design lessons worth copying from Orca's comments, both learned the hard way there:
- It keeps the title layer and the agent-hook layer as SEPARATE evidence, because consumers combine them differently, and a single merged status silently changes behaviour.
- 'Evidence that something runs is not proof of who': it splits activity classification from agent identity, since a bare spinner says something is working but not what. Do not collapse the two.

Relationship to nocx-5mn.4 (OSC 133): complementary, not competing. OSC 133 D marks SHELL command boundaries — the build finished, claude exited. Title status covers what happens INSIDE one long-running command, which is exactly the Claude Code case OSC 133 cannot see. Build both; they answer different questions.
close_reason: Solved by the title-status layer: a braille spinner means working, Claude Code's ✳ means waiting, and a waiting background tab lights the underline. The OSC 133 dependency was my own modelling error — those markers are complementary (they cover shell command boundaries, which cannot see inside a long-running agent) and remain as nocx-5mn.4, not a blocker for this.

title: Tab title goes blank when a TUI exits (empty OSC 0/2 is taken literally)
description: Run claude code in a tab and exit it: the tab label becomes empty. title: [bake-off] ghostty-web: seams between cells on Retina — canvas-2d fills fractional cell rects, no font size avoids it
description: Big block glyphs render with a visible grid of seams in the ghostty-web tab; xterm.js draws the same art solid. Cause: ghostty-web does ctx.scale(devicePixelRatio) then fillRect(x, y, metrics.width, metrics.height) in CSS pixels, so every cell edge lands between physical pixels and gets antialiased. Reproduced in isolation without WASM: adjacent fillRects of 8.4 CSS px at DPR 2 show seams, 9.0 CSS px are solid. Not fixable by configuration — the font stack's advance/fontSize ratio is 0.6021, so no integer font size from 12 to 20 yields an integer device-pixel cell width. There is also no WebGL path to switch to: the library contains zero webgl/gpu references, canvas-2d only. Same root class as nocx-4wk (blur from imageSmoothing/DPR). Fixing it would mean patching ghostty-web to snap cell metrics to whole device pixels.
notes: CORRECTION: 'not fixable by configuration' was wrong — only integer font sizes were tested. The advance is exactly linear (0.60205em/cell), so fractional sizes do land the cell on whole device pixels: 14.12 -> 17.002 device px, 16.61 -> 20.000 device px at DPR 2. FONT_SIZE set to 14.12 to test. Still unverified: cell HEIGHT (horizontal seams) is derived from font metrics/LINE_HEIGHT and was not measured, and this uses measureText('M') which may differ from ghostty-web's internal metric. Also note the deeper option: ghostty-web's WASM core exposes a full renderer-facing API (getLine/getViewport/isRowDirty/markClean/needsFullRedraw/getCursor/getColors), so a custom WebGL renderer on top of the ghostty VT core is possible — it just means writing from scratch what xterm.js's WebglAddon already provides.
close_reason: ghostty-web dropped from the project (user decision 2026-07-21). These three bugs are ghostty-web-specific rendering defects (imageSmoothing/DPR blur, Retina cell seams from fractional canvas-2d rects, scroll reset on new output) and no longer describe any code we ship. xterm.js is the VT frontend per ADR-0001.

title: [bake-off] ghostty-web resets scroll position to bottom on new output

title: [bug] Resize forwarded to PTY on every intermediate grid size — SIGWINCH storm shreds TUIs
description: tabs.ts forwarded every renderer onResize straight to ws.sendResize with no debounce and no dedupe, so dragging a window edge walks the PTY through every intermediate grid size. Each one is a SIGWINCH and a full TUI repaint for a size that is already stale — visible as the screen falling apart during resize, identically in all three renderers (shared code, not the engines). Fix: skip unchanged cols/rows and debounce the PTY notification by RESIZE_SETTLE_MS (80ms); local fitting stays immediate.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging the window edge produces one PTY resize on settle, not one per intermediate size; TUI redraws cleanly
close_reason: Fixed in frontend/src/tabs.ts: dedupe unchanged grid sizes + 80ms trailing debounce before notifying the PTY.

title: [bug] WS frames decoded with a fresh TextDecoder — split UTF-8 sequences become U+FFFD
description: ipc.ts decoded every WebSocket frame with 'new TextDecoder().decode(buf)'. A PTY read ends at an arbitrary byte offset, so multi-byte UTF-8 routinely straddles two frames; a per-frame decoder severs the sequence and emits U+FFFD for each half. U+FFFD renders as a question mark in a diamond, identically in every renderer, so it reads as a font/glyph bug and sent the renderer bake-off chasing ghosts. Reproduced live against the real PTY+WS: braille art through a 40-col PTY gave 10x U+FFFD with the old path, 0 with a single streaming decoder. Fix: one TextDecoder per connection, decode(buf, {stream:true}).
acceptance_criteria: Multi-byte UTF-8 split across WS frames renders intact; verified end-to-end against a live PTY
close_reason: Fixed in frontend/src/ipc.ts: one TextDecoder per connection with {stream:true}. Verified end-to-end against a live PTY — 10x U+FFFD before, 0 after.

title: [bug] PTY inherits no locale when app is launched from Finder → TUIs downgrade UTF-8 to '?'
description: pty_local.go sets only TERM: cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "TERM=xterm-256color"). A macOS .app launched from Finder/Dock has no LANG/LC_* in its environment, so the child shell has no locale. Python/Rich/prompt_toolkit TUIs then compute a non-UTF-8 stdout encoding and encode with errors='replace', which emits literal '?' bytes for every non-ASCII glyph — identical in every renderer, so it masquerades as a font bug. Launching via 'wails dev' from a terminal hides this because LANG is inherited. Fix: default LANG/LC_CTYPE to a UTF-8 locale in NewLocal when absent.
acceptance_criteria: Shell spawned by a Finder-launched nocx.app reports a UTF-8 locale; non-ASCII TUI output renders without '?' substitution
close_reason: Fixed in internal/pty/pty_local.go: withUTF8Locale() defaults LANG=en_US.UTF-8 when the inherited environment states no locale at all (LC_ALL/LC_CTYPE/LANG all absent), which is the Finder/Dock launch case. An inherited locale is never overridden, including a deliberate LANG=C. Table-driven test covers all five cases; go test -race, gofumpt and golangci-lint all green.
